question: Sicily is facing issues with financial management, its autonomy (as enshrined in the Treaty on European Union (TEU)1) and the non-implementation of its regional statute.

This state of affairs clashes starkly with the EU’s goal to achieve economic and social cohesion, as well as its aims laid down in Article 174 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, which states that particular attention must be paid to islands and cross-border regions in order to reduce development disparities.

More specifically, the region has been stripped of its basic right to levy taxes, of the entitlement of its financial offices to set and collect taxes, and of tax revenue enshrined in the Statute, resulting in a structural imbalance in the region’s finances.

Worryingly, the Italian State is also planning to transfer the tax revenue earned in the region to the most prosperous part of the country, disregarding the basic service standards set in the Constitution2 – a move that will widen the development gap further. Is the Commission willing to: 1.
examine Italy’s financial management practices in relation to Sicily to determine their compatibility with the EU’s principles of regional development and cohesion and with the region’s autonomy?
assess actual implementation of the Sicilian Statute and the effect that the restrictions imposed are having on Sicily’s autonomy?
give details of corrective measures that will put an end to the discrimination Sicily has faced so that it can exercise its autonomy in full?
Article 4(2) TEU. Article 119 of the Constitution.
answer: EN E-658/24 on behalf of the European Commission (26.4.2024) It is not for the Commission to assess the administrative organisation of Member States in relation to their constitutional order or to the way taxation competences are distributed among the various levels of government.
